parsed.rationale: The structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning these two protocols share no members at all. `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` (in `Shared/Playback/Sources/HLSPlayer/Protocol/HLSAVPlayerProtocol.swift`) exposes low-level AVFoundation primitives (`currentTime`, `rate`, `seekableTimeRanges`, `seek:(to time: CMTime)`) while `TimeShiftablePlayer` (in `Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/TimeShiftablePlayer.swift`) exposes a higher-level domain API (`secondsBehindLive`, `seekToLive`, `stateStream`, `eventStream`, `makeAudioBufferStream`). The only surface overlap is the bare `play:()` method name, which is a coincidental vocabulary match across two distinct abstraction layers — one wrapping AVPlayer internals and one describing time-shift playback semantics. Introducing a parent protocol would create a forced abstraction with no shared contract to express, coupling an HLS-transport-layer protocol to a domain-level player protocol without benefit.
